## Welcome {.unnumbered}

::: {.column-margin}
![](/vol4/parts/images/stack_vol4.svg){width=100% fig-alt="Three-tier Physical AI stack: the Brain proposes learned actions, the Nervous System checks timing and permission, and the Body actuates within physical limits. The causal boundary marks admission to force and motion."}

*The three-tier Physical AI stack: the Brain proposes learned actions, the Nervous System checks timing and permission, and the Body actuates within physical limits.*
:::

Physical artificial intelligence begins where computation ceases to be symbolic and becomes physical force. For an engineer trained in machine learning systems—accustomed to distributed training clusters, PyTorch and JAX graph compilation, memory hierarchies, and batch inference—physical AI represents a profound architectural shift. In digital systems, hardware is an abstract execution substrate where a failed execution triggers an exception handler and a wrong prediction is discarded with near-zero physical cost. In physical systems, software commands mass, momentum, and energy across the causal boundary. A mispredicted token costs milliseconds of accelerator time; a mistimed torque command dissipates irreversible energy into mechanical plant, where momentum cannot be paused and stopping distance cannot be reclaimed.

Because physical reality admits no software rollbacks, physical AI cannot be treated as a pure statistical scaling problem. Adding parameters or pretraining tokens does not alter the speed of light, motor winding resistance, or Coulomb friction. Engineering dependable embodied intelligence requires partitioning the machine by authority and execution timescale. As illustrated in the architecture stack, the machine is organized into three cooperating tiers: the cognitive Brain proposes learned actions, the deterministic Nervous System validates timing and permits or refuses proposals on isolated real-time silicon, and the physical Body actuates within strict physical limits at the causal boundary.

## The Volume IV Thesis {.unnumbered}

The central thesis of Volume IV is that physical AI is an architectural discipline governed by physical conservation laws, hard real-time deadlines, and the causal irreversibility of work. Because statistical scaling of neural parameters cannot alter momentum, thermal limits, or stopping distance, dependable embodied intelligence demands an architectural separation of concerns: high-capacity neural networks propose actions, while a deterministic permission path enforces physical invariants on isolated real-time silicon.

In digital machine learning, empirical scaling laws demonstrate that expanding model capacity and pretraining data reliably drives down test cross-entropy. In physical systems, however, statistical scaling hits a hard physical wall. Deep neural networks are stochastic function approximators that optimize average-case loss over training distributions, whereas physical safety is a worst-case tail phenomenon where an unhandled failure causes irreversible collision or structural damage. Furthermore, physical interaction is closed-loop and endogenous ($s_{t+1} \sim P(s \mid s_t, a_t)$), causing imitation errors to compound quadratically over the planning horizon ($\mathcal{O}(T^2 \epsilon)$). Finally, physical conservation laws are non-negotiable: a foundation model cannot brake harder than tire-floor Coulomb friction allows, nor can it bypass motor thermal dissipation envelopes ($P = I^2 R$). Safety cannot be solved inside neural network weights; it must be enforced by systems architecture.

## The Capstone Architecture and Curriculum Arc {.unnumbered}

Across seventeen chapters, Volume IV develops this thesis through a continuous engineering progression centered on two capstone reference machines: the warehouse mobile manipulator and the bipedal humanoid. Every chapter adds an explicit term to the machine's physical budget, tracing how raw physics, learned policies, and deterministic execution converge into a certifiable physical system:

* **Introduction: The Causal Boundary** (@sec-boundary) defines the causal boundary where digital commands become physical work and establishes the five-level machine model that organizes the volume.
* **Part I: The Machine Anatomy** (@sec-body, @sec-brain, @sec-nervous) turns the first bedrock law, physical irreversibility, into coupled budgets of time, distance, torque, heat, and voltage across the Body, Brain, and Nervous System.
* **Part II: Teaching the Machine** (@sec-data, @sec-training, @sec-evaluation) confronts the second law, endogenous data, establishing closed-loop data collection, imitation policy training, and adversarial evaluation under compounding distribution shift.
* **Part III: Running the Machine** (@sec-perception, @sec-memory, @sec-intent, @sec-planning, @sec-enforcement, @sec-placement) implements the third law, proposal is not permission, orchestrating multi-rate runtime execution from 1 Hz semantic intent down to 20 kHz motor control, and enforcing Control Barrier Functions while isolating system-on-chip (SoC) memory crossbars.
* **Part IV: Governing the Machine** (@sec-intervention, @sec-verification, @sec-release) applies the fourth law, evidence bounds authority, establishing supervisory human handovers, hardware-in-the-loop fault injection, and certifiable deployment release cases grounded in empirical limit records.
* **Capstone Synthesis: The Epistemic Frontier** (@sec-frontier) integrates the complete architecture, answering what the machine can guarantee and logging open premises in an accountable residual-claims register.

:::
